task:
BUILD F2D PR3: the on-demand archetype explanation endpoint. Base on current origin/main (record the SHA; it must include F2d PR2, merged as #810 at 6c7bf95a704ebef4d3f18d48acff9ec47cffe639). New branch, no target_branch.

AUTHORITY: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-v3-finder-f2d-wide-archetype-and-product-attachment-design.md. Read CLAUDE.md first, then design section 4 in full (4.1 endpoint and shared model, 4.2 read and compute path, 4.3 exact version rule), section 5.1 (the two shared SQL read constants and the two digests), and the PR3 bullet in section 10. Where this task and the design differ, the design wins. Where the design and the current code differ, follow the design and name the conflict in your summary. Owner approval for the additive route (design question 4) and the exact-version 409 rule (question 5) is recorded in docs/operations/v3-finder-capacity-decision-2026-10-10.md section 5.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (PR1 #809, PR2 #810 -- read these before coding): shared_contracts/v3_system_archetype_model.py is the canonical model with score_raw_system(vector_row, opportunity_groups), VECTOR_READ_SQL and OPPORTUNITY_READ_SQL (psycopg %(name)s parameters: generation_id, chunk_ordinal, system_id64), the _explain_anchored/_explain_flexible functions, confidence_to_ppm, completeness_to_ppm, weighted_key_e4, ARCHETYPE_VERSION = 'v3-archetype-4' and archetype_model_sha256(); apps/api/src/local_search.py has _current_derived_generation(), which already returns archetype_version, archetype_manifest_sha256 and archetype_model_sha256 from the published product row and fails closed with 503 unless both Finder products are READY and published; routers/archetypes.py already runs its ranked read inside `async with conn.transaction(isolation='repeatable_read', readonly=True)` (around line 391) -- mirror that pattern; v3_app.system_archetype is the wide row (eight <key>_score/_tier/_confidence_ppm/_weighted_e4 groups, completeness_ppm, summary columns) visible only for the current PUBLISHED generation's READY and published product. The API uses asyncpg ($1 placeholders) while the shared SQL constants use psycopg %(name)s style: convert the two constants to asyncpg placeholders mechanically at import time (a small, tested helper that replaces each named parameter with $n in a fixed order) rather than rewriting the SQL text, so the route reads through the SAME query contracts the builder uses (design 4.2 forbids rewriting them).

ALLOWED FILES: apps/api/src/routers/archetypes.py (the new route and its helpers only; the legacy GET /api/archetypes/system/{id64} stays UNCHANGED, as do /rankings, /rerank, /simulate, /profiles); apps/api/src/models.py (the new response models); apps/api/src/local_search.py only if a shared helper must be exported; shared_contracts/v3_system_archetype_model.py only to add an explanation-assembly helper that calls the existing _explain_* functions (do not touch the scoring functions, the SQL constants or the digest walk -- the digest must stay byte-identical, and a test must prove archetype_model_sha256() is unchanged by your edit); the regenerated clients apps/web/src/lib/api/generated/types.gen.ts, apps/web/src/lib/api/generated/sdk.gen.ts and packages/api-client/src/generated/api.gen.ts (cd apps/web && pnpm generate:api; if the runner lacks pnpm/Node say so and list the schema additions); tests/test_archetype_system_v3.py (new), tests/test_ranking_identity_and_no_legacy.py, tests/test_v3_system_archetype_model.py (digest-unchanged proof), tests/integration/conftest.py and tests/ratings_v4_pg_fixture.py only if the fixture needs a published wide row for these tests; CHANGES.md. Any other changed path must be justified in your summary as required by a specific failing test, otherwise it is a failure.

ENDPOINT (design 4.1): GET /api/archetypes/system/{id64}/explanation. Path parameter id64: Path(ge=0, le=9223372036854775807) -- a negative or over-bigint value is a 422, never an asyncpg encoding failure. Three optional identity query parameters: expected_generation_id: uuid.UUID | None; expected_archetype_version: Query(None, min_length=1, max_length=128); expected_manifest_sha256: Query(None, pattern=r'^[0-9a-f]{64}$'). A malformed value is a 422 from validation, never a 409 and never a database parameter. When any is supplied and differs from the current published product, answer 409 with the exact detail of 4.3; a 200 always echoes the identity it computed against (the shared ranking identity block: ranking_version, ranking_sha256, derived_generation_id, publication_sequence, archetype_version, archetype_manifest_sha256, archetype_model_sha256).

EXACT VERSION RULE (design 4.3), checked BEFORE reading inputs or calling the model: serve only when v3_meta.derived_product.product_version == the stored row's archetype_version == the deployed shared model's ARCHETYPE_VERSION, AND sha256 of the deployed shared_contracts/v3_system_archetype_model.py file == the product manifest's model_file_sha256, AND the product is READY and published on the current PUBLISHED generation (the existing _current_derived_generation() 503 covers the last part). The API hashes its deployed model file ONCE at start-up (module import), not per request. On any mismatch return HTTP 409 with the exact detail string: explanation unavailable for this product version

READ AND COMPUTE PATH (design 4.2): one read-only REPEATABLE READ transaction holds the identity check, the identity-parameter comparison and the data read, so a publication committing mid-request is invisible (serve entirely from one snapshot or 409, never a mix). Inside it, for the current generation and the requested id64: read the one system_rating_vector row and the integer opportunity groups through the two shared constants narrowed by their system_id64 parameter (chunk_ordinal NULL), and the one generation-pinned v3_app.system_archetype wide row. Wide row absent -> 404. Otherwise call score_raw_system, build the eight explanations from the same inputs via the _explain_* functions, and compare EVERY recomputed value -- the eight scores, tiers and confidence ppm, completeness_ppm, all eight <key>_weighted_e4 keys, primary/secondary archetype, best_colony_potential, best_tier, archetype_confidence_ppm, weighted_potential -- with the stored row; on ANY mismatch fail closed with a 5xx (choose 503 with a detail that names the mismatched column, and log it) -- an explanation never describes a different stored score or ranking key. Return per-archetype entries (key, score, tier, confidence (ppm/1e6), weighted_e4, explanation dict) plus the summary and completeness, and the identity block. Cost must stay two index probes plus eight in-process fits: no scan of the product or the galaxy, nothing stored.

MODELS (apps/api/src/models.py): new Pydantic response models with extra='forbid' like their neighbours; reuse the existing RankingIdentity model for the identity block; the explanation dict may be typed loosely (dict[str, Any]) since its shape belongs to the model module. Regenerate the three typed clients.

TESTS (tests/test_archetype_system_v3.py, disposable PostgreSQL 18 through the fixtures the PR1/PR2 ranking tests use -- a published wide row built through the real builder; runners have no PostgreSQL, so write them, run everything that runs without a database and list the database tests you wrote but could not run): both path bounds (-1 and 2**63 -> 422, 0 and 2**63-1 accepted); an over-128 and an empty expected_archetype_version -> 422; 63- and 65-character, upper-case and non-hex expected_manifest_sha256 -> 422; a supplied expected identity that differs from the published product -> 409 with the exact string; with the model patched: a READY published product whose version differs -> 409 with the exact string and the model NOT called (assert via a spy); versions equal but model_file_sha256 differing -> the same 409; matching -> 200 with all eight explanations and values identical to the stored row, and the identity block echoed; wide row absent -> 404; a seeded divergent stored completeness_ppm and, separately, one divergent <key>_weighted_e4 -> the fail-closed response (patch or direct UPDATE under a BUILDING product on a disposable DB, however the fixture permits); a publication committed from a second connection between the identity statement and the data statement -> a response consistent with exactly one snapshot (use a barrier/patch between the two statements); the legacy GET /api/archetypes/system/{id64} is byte-for-byte unchanged (static assertion on the source range or its tests still passing); the digest-unchanged proof in tests/test_v3_system_archetype_model.py (archetype_model_sha256() equals the value recorded before your edit -- record it in the test as a constant); and tests/test_ranking_identity_and_no_legacy.py extended so the new route reads no legacy relation.

VALIDATION TO RUN AND REPORT WITH EXACT COUNTS: ruff check apps/api/src shared_contracts tests; python -m pytest tests/test_v3_system_archetype_model.py tests/test_ranking_profile_identity.py tests/test_ranking_sql.py -q -p no:warnings; every other touched module that runs without a database; pnpm generate:api and the git status of the generated files if the toolchain is available. Parameterized SQL only; fail-closed; no deploy, no production access, no production credentials.

IF YOU CANNOT FINISH EVERYTHING IN THIS SESSION, complete in this order and stop cleanly: route + version rule + 404/409/503 contracts, models, client regeneration, tests. State precisely what remains. End with: files changed; tests run with counts; database tests written but not run; whether the clients were regenerated; the archetype_model_sha256 value before and after your change (they must be equal); and any design-versus-code conflict you found.
